## Verdict

wrong

## Bearer

DisplayFormatter.formatDateRelative — core-domain/src/main/kotlin/com/mgilli/core/domain/display/DisplayFormatter.kt

## Trigger

ProfileViewModel.syncStatusText calling DisplayFormatter.formatDateRelative(lastSyncSuccessAt, clock.now()) — observed

## Today

formatDateRelative compares the local calendar date of `instant` against
the local calendar date of `now`. It only tests for equality (Today) and
for exactly one day before (Yesterday); any other case, including
`instant`'s date being after `now`'s date, falls into the `else` branch
and returns `DateDisplay.Earlier`, the same value used for a date that is
genuinely long past. A stored sync instant ahead of now — from a clock
that stepped back or from drift between the phone and the watch — is
rendered exactly like an old sync, through `ProfileViewModel.syncStatusText`
and `PhoneStringResources.Profile.lastSyncEarlier`. No test in
DisplayFormatterTest.kt exercises an `instant` after `now`.

## Expected

formatDateRelative checks whether `instant`'s local date is after
`now`'s local date and returns a value distinct from `Earlier` for that
case, rather than falling through to it. `DateDisplay` is a sealed class
with exactly three subtypes (Today, Yesterday, Earlier); representing a
future instant distinctly requires either a new subtype or reusing
`Today` for a date not in the past, and either choice changes the `when`
in `ProfileViewModel.syncStatusText` (lines 237-241), which is exhaustive
over the three current subtypes today and would need a branch added if a
subtype is added.
